content:
maria: Quick question — spinning up a temporary dev cluster in us-east for integration tests with a vendor SFTP. Need outbound egress to a single IP and want security sign-off + logging redaction guidance. IP: 203.0.113.55. Plan: add SG outbound 22 to that IP from the cluster NAT, enable VPC endpoint for S3 so artifacts don't egress, and ensure app/logs don't record S3 object keys. Can security confirm this is ok and any additional reqs? (will be live for ~48h)

ashley: @maria thanks — couple Qs: 1) is that vendor IP stable? 2) will we be sending filenames in SFTP payload or only metadata? 3) we need to avoid CloudTrail data events logging object keys (S3) — are you using S3 PUTs with object names?

maria: Vendor confirmed single static IP (203.0.113.55). We will upload test tarballs to s3://redwood-dev-integ/<job-id>/<artifact>.tar.gz — so object keys include job-id/artifact names. App currently logs object key on success; I can remove key from logs. No downstream consumers need keys in plain logs.

samir: Network side: SG/NAT change is fine for 48h but prefer to lock source to the cluster subnet. Suggest creating a short-lived allowlist rule on the NAT's outbound SG: TCP 22 to 203.0.113.55/32, annotate with ticket # for audit. Also toggle VPC endpoint for S3 so traffic stays in AWS.

jordan: For CloudTrail data events — they do capture object-level events including keys if enabled. We don't have data events enabled on the dev bucket, right? If we enable for testing we need to redact or avoid storing keys in plain logs. Ash: if you don't need object-level audit, don't enable data events for that bucket.

ashley: +1 to not enabling CloudTrail S3 data events for dev bucket. App-level logging must be sanitized. If we must capture object names for debugging, write to a restricted log group that auto-expires and is KMS-encrypted.

maria: Ok I'll patch app to stop logging keys, and if we need debugging I'll send them to a temp log group with 30d retention and restricted perms. I'll open a ticket with details and the 48h window.

samir: Please include the following in the ticket: CIDR of cluster (10.40.8.0/24), exact start/end times, justification, and owner. I'll apply the ephemeral SG rule and add an "expires_at" tag. Example SG rule we’ll add:
```
Type: Outbound
Protocol: TCP
Port range: 22
Destination: 203.0.113.55/32
Source: sg-xxxxxxxx (cluster NAT SG)
Expiration tag: expires_at=2026-03-19T18:00:00Z
```

sec-bot: Security checklist reminder: ensure S3 bucket has encryption at rest, no public access, server-side encryption, and enable VPC endpoint policy restricting to bucket prefix. Also confirm logs do not contain PII — redact user ids if present. :shield:

maria: Thanks all — I'll remove key logging now, create the ticket, and post the ticket number here. Appreciate the quick reviews :thumbsup:
